findings.disposition_reason: the figcaption states the nesting explicitly and the evidence table below the figure marks the same three rows with an arrow prefix, so the reader is warned before summing; not worth a redraw
findings.summary: The three subparts of the fresh-geometry branch (stencil construction, geometry channel calls, closing contraction) are drawn as ordinary sibling rows: the two-space indent carried in the label strings is invisible because matplotlib right-aligns tick labels, so the picture alone gives no cue that those three bars compose the 'Fresh geometry, whole' bar above them. A reader who sums every row will double-count. The figcaption states 'do not add its whole row to its subparts', so the nesting is recoverable from the caption rather than from the image.

findings.disposition_reason: the extra digit carries real signal on bars too short to read off the axis, and the evidence table gives all values to three decimals for anyone comparing precisely
findings.summary: Value annotation precision switches with magnitude: two decimals at or above 1 ms (2.64, 13.34) and three below it (0.285, 0.303, 0.267). The labels are the only way to read the sub-millisecond rows because the linear axis renders those bars a few pixels long, so a reader comparing a small row against a large one is comparing different precision.

RUBRIC data_ink: pass - the bars are the only marks; no gradient, fill or shading is drawn and the printed values do not compete with them
RUBRIC decoration: pass - white background, no gridlines, top/right/left spines removed, frameless legend in clear space above the plot
RUBRIC contrast: pass - near-black part names and #333333 value labels on white, and both bar colours clear 3:1 against the background

RUBRIC table_form: pass - the eight parts are a decomposition of one quantity across two batch sizes, so paired bars show relative magnitude that a table would not; it is not a list of independent facts
